name: Nebraska
summary: The state seal in gold and silver on a blue field. The seal shows a blacksmith with a hammer and anvil, a settler's cabin, sheaves of wheat, a steamboat on the Missouri River, a train toward the Rocky Mountains, and the motto 'Equality before the law'.
origin: The design was adopted as the state banner in 1925 and designated the official state flag in 1963.

symbols.name: Blacksmith
symbols.description: A smith working at an anvil.

symbols.description: A cabin and sheaves of wheat.

symbols.name: Steamboat and train
symbols.description: A steamboat on the river and a train toward the mountains.

facts: In a 2001 NAVA survey it ranked among the lowest-rated state flag designs.
Its seal includes the date of statehood, 1 March 1867.
The legislature has considered redesigns several times.
clues: A gold and silver seal on blue with a blacksmith, a cabin, a steamboat and a train.
Its motto is 'Equality before the law'.
It was a state banner before becoming the state flag in 1963.
